title: Prairie Avenue, summer 1904

lighting.note: Mid-morning, 1 July 1904, in local mean solar time at the datum (the city's clocks then kept Central Standard Time, about ten minutes behind it). Chosen for the view the scene opens on: the visitor faces west-south-west across Prairie Avenue at the Glessner lot, so a sun still in the east-south-east lights the Prairie Avenue fronts and the ground in front of them rather than leaving them in their own shadow, as a noon or afternoon sun would.

anchors.label: Prairie at Eighteenth, facing the Glessner lot at 1800 Prairie

note: The second scene (T-1739, piece 2 of T-1252), on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-26 that the Prairie Avenue scene serves 1904. It stands on e1871_postfire: T-1251's zone table, generated and baked by T-1738 over E +1100..+1800, N -3800..-2900, with the lake at T-1250's scene line. THE SPAWN AND `glessner_house` ARE ONE POSE, derived rather than chosen. The crossing of Prairie Avenue and E. 18th Street is the sheet-28 control point of data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json (E 1401.86, N -3206.60, through that file's fitted similarity), and both streets are 66 ft wide as sheet 28 prints them, so the street lines stand 33 ft either side of it along the sheet's own axes (Prairie runs at bearing 178.99). The Glessner lot's north-east street corner is then E 1391.98, N -3216.83, and the lot centroid, from the rectangle in data/research/glessner_house_1904_spec.json § lot.corners_lot_m (T-1731; 53.63 x 23.47 m), is E 1365.37, N -3229.04. The visitor stands on the EAST sidewalk at the corner, 2.0 m inside Prairie's east street line and 1.5 m south of 18th Street's south line (E 1410.12, N -3218.01); those two offsets are a camera, not a claim about the walk. T-0474's grid lays the walk 0.30-2.13 m inside the street line (the 1905 code's one-foot set-back, sec. 2062, and a reconstructed 6-ft walk, docs/LIBERTIES.md L292), so the camera stands on it; its material is T-1728's. The yaw bisects the bearings from there to the lot's street corner (273.72) and to its centroid (256.15), so the corner stands right of centre and the body of the lot left of it, both inside a phone's 390 x 780 frame. The house itself is T-1729's and is not drawn yet; the label names the lot, which is what the selected year contains and what the model can show. The layers list is the renderer's contract (T-1739): this scene draws its own ground and water, the 1904 street grid (T-0474: data/street_grid/1904.json, carriageways, block faces, alleys and the Prairie Avenue lots read off Sanborn 1911 sheets 20, 28 and 35), and none of the 1835 town's layers (streets, fences, signs, goods, walks, docks, boats, wells, plants, trees, the residents' directory), all of which are authored for 1 July 1835. No structure record resolves at 1904, so no building is placed. tools/measure_anchors.mjs holds the pose against the e1871 heightfield.
